concerns.location: plan.md:Semantic coherence definition and ANCOVA modeling (section 'Technical Context' and Phase 4)
concerns.text: The metric *semantic coherence* is computed as the mean pairwise cosine similarity of sentence‑level embeddings (mean(pairwise_cosine(embeddings))). This statistic is sensitive to the number of sentences (K_i) per participant because the averaging denominator varies with K_i. Participants with fewer sentences (common in more severe cognitive impairment) will have a different bias in the coherence estimate, creating a confound between the predictor (coherence) and disease status. The current plan does not include sentence count (or total word count) as a covariate or otherwise adjust for this dependency, risking a spurious association in the ANCOVA. This undermines the claim that the coherence metric independently reflects linguistic degradation.

concerns.location: plan.md:Phase 4 – ANCOVA assumptions (section 'Phase 4 – Feature Extraction & Statistical Testing')
concerns.text: The plan relies on ANCOVA assumptions of normality and homogeneity of regression slopes but does not specify how violations will be handled beyond reporting them. With a modest sample size (~300) and a derived metric that may be non‑normally distributed, a parametric ANCOVA may be inappropriate. Consider pre‑testing normality and, if violated, using a non‑parametric alternative (e.g., permutation‑based ANCOVA) or transforming the coherence scores.
